answer: Each identity posts a ferrous bond that rusts: its value decays each epoch unless renewed by attestations. Renewal needs vouching from three disjoint knoll clusters, and each knoll prices its vouch slots convexly in how many identities it has already vouched for, so the marginal cost of the Nth clone rises with N. An onyx audit samples identities by verifiable randomness; if one clone fails, every identity sharing its vouch path is slashed together, so N clones risk N squared in forfeited bonds. Honest users renew cheaply; attackers buy scarce, pricier vouching while facing correlated ruin.
